# local 0007: mcs51: reads such as *a[1][1] through an element of a nested array of pointers in data memory first store the pointer through itself

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Do not let geniCodeDerefPtr set isaddr on the result operand of the iCode that geniCodeRValue has just emitted.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For `rdl` and `rdc` below, the compiler emits a store of the pointer through itself in front of
the read. The file was compiled on r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 p2.c` and run in ucsim.

```c
long v = 0x11223344;
char buf[3] = { 0x55, 0x66, 0x77 };
long *a[2][2];
struct s { char c; char *names[2]; } st;

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[9];

long rdl (void) { return *a[1][1]; }
char rdc (void) { return *st.names[1]; }

void main (void)
{
  unsigned char i;

  a[1][1] = &v;
  st.names[1] = buf;
  res[0] = (rdl () == 0x11223344);
  res[1] = rdc ();
  for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
    res[2 + i] = ((unsigned char *)&v)[i];
  for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
    res[6 + i] = buf[i];
  for (;;);
}
```

After the run `res` holds `00 0c 08 00 40 11 0c 00 40`, and `01 55 44 33 22 11 55 66 77` is
expected. `v` is at address 0x08 and `buf` at 0x0c, so the three bytes of each generic pointer
have replaced the first three bytes of the object that it points to. `rdl` loads the pointer into
`dptr` and `b`, calls `__gptrput` three times with the bytes of the pointer, and then reads with
`__gptrget`.

`--stack-auto` gives this result too. With `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto` the result is the expected one, because the arrays are not in data
memory. For `long * __data adl[2][2];` the compiler emits the three calls with `--model-medium`
and `--model-large` as well, which was compiled and not run.

Other expressions were compiled with the small model and read in the assembly. The store is
present for `*a[0][0]`, for a three-dimensional array, for elements that point to `int` or
`char`, and for `*sa[1].names[1]`. For elements of the type `__data long *` it is
`mov @r0,(_ad + 0x0003)`. It is absent for a one-dimensional array `long *a1[4]`, for `*a[1][i]`
with a variable index, for `a[1][1][2]`, for elements of the type `__xdata long *`, and for the
write `*a[1][1] = 5`.

## Cause

The cause was read from the source and from the iCode that `--dump-i-code` writes. No patch was
tried.

For unary `*`, `ast2iCode` in `src/SDCCicode.c` calls
`geniCodeDerefPtr (geniCodeRValue (left, false), lvl)`. For an element operand that
`geniCodeArray` made, `geniCodeRValue` emits the `GET_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` that reads the pointer
and returns the result operand of that iCode itself. `geniCodeDerefPtr` sets `isaddr` on the
operand that it is given, so the flag is set in the iCode. For other pointer operands
`geniCodeRValue` returns a copy. In the iCode for `*a[1][1]` the result of the first read has
`isaddr` set, and for `*a1[1]` it does not.

In `src/mcs51/ralloc.c`, an iTemp whose only definition is a read through a near pointer that can
be rematerialized becomes a pseudo symbol at that address. `ptrPseudoSymConvert` in
`src/SDCCptropt.c` changes the read to the assignment `iTemp = iTemp`. With `isaddr` set on the
result, the macro `POINTER_SET` holds for this assignment, and the code generator emits a store
through the pointer. After register allocation the iCode for `*a[1][1]` has
`*(iTemp3) := iTemp3`, and the iCode for `*a1[1]` has `iTemp2 := iTemp2`.
`src/ds390/ralloc.c` also calls `ptrPseudoSymConvert` for such iTemps. ds390 was not tested.

## Related

Bug #2691 concerns the address of such elements, `&a[i][j]`. This defect was found with its test
cases, and its patch does not change it.
